content:
Numbers up to 1000 is the backbone of the Class 2 Maths Olympiad — place value, expanded form and ordering appear in almost every IMO and SOF paper. This guide covers what the chapter tests, the facts a Class 2 child needs, the slips that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test drawn from our verified question bank.

What the Class 2 Maths Olympiad Numbers (0–1000) chapter tests

  • Place value — reading a 3-digit number as hundreds, tens and ones
  • Expanded and standard form, and number names to 1000
  • Comparing and ordering 3-digit numbers with <, > and =
  • Skip counting, ordinal numbers and odd/even

Key facts your child should know

  • A three-digit number is hundreds + tens + ones: 346 = 300 + 40 + 6.
  • To compare, look at the hundreds first, then tens, then ones. So 642 > 624.
  • Skip counting by 100 keeps the tens and ones the same: 100, 200, 300…
  • Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8; odd in 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Writing the expanded form with the wrong place values (e.g. 40 instead of 4 for the tens digit).
  • Comparing the ones before the hundreds when ordering.
  • Confusing the ordinal (3rd) with the number of items (3).

quiz.title: IMO Class 2 Numbers (0–1000) Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Veer starts at 578 and counts on 7 tens. Which number does Veer reach?
In a race, Riya finishes just after the 7th runner. What is Riya's position?
questions.explanation: Just after the 7th runner means one place later, so Riya is 8th.
Ascending order means smallest to largest: 343, 345, 354, 435.

questions.q: What is the 2nd letter of the word PENCIL?
questions.explanation: Count the letters of PENCIL from the left: the 2nd letter is E.
Nine hundred two means 9 hundreds, 0 tens and 2 ones, which is 902.

questions.q: Write "five hundred twenty-four" as a numeral.
questions.explanation: Five hundred twenty-four means 5 hundreds, 2 tens and 4 ones, which is 524.

questions.q: Continue the pattern 236, 336, 436, … What is the next number?
questions.explanation: The numbers grow by 100 each time, so 436 + 100 = 536.

questions.q: A 3-digit number has 8 in the ones place. Is the number odd or even?
options: Cannot say without the other digits
questions.explanation: Only the ones digit decides odd or even. 8 is even, so the number is even.

questions.q: Veer counts back 4 ones from 502. Which number does Veer land on?

faq.q: What is place value for Class 2?
faq.a: It is the value a digit has because of its position. In 346 the 3 is worth 300 (hundreds), the 4 is 40 (tens) and the 6 is 6 (ones).
Compare the hundreds digit first. The number with more hundreds is bigger; if equal, compare tens, then ones.
